k3_acceptance_analysis.interpretation: K=3 is not failing uniformly. The first draft token is accepted at roughly K=1 quality, but the second and third speculative positions collapse. This points to multi-step distribution drift/exposure bias in math CoT decoding: once a draft prefix diverges even slightly from the target model trajectory, deeper speculative tokens are much less likely to match exact verifier tokens.
k3_acceptance_analysis.operational_decision: Treat K=1 as the current production-quality setting for NeMo-RL. K=2/K=3 should only be enabled behind adaptive depth or long-tail gating if per-position acceptance improves.

adaptive_gate_implementation.scope: Taming Long Tail/ReSpec-style adaptive activation and draft-depth selection for NeMo-RL/vLLM SpecDec
adaptive_gate_implementation.current_behavior: The vLLM scheduler lookahead gate starts from static request/token thresholds, measures local SpecDec enabled ratios over rolling windows, then tightens or loosens request/token thresholds toward a target enabled ratio. The scheduler request pressure now uses active requests, max(len(self.running), scheduled_requests), instead of scheduled_requests alone, so long-tail activation follows the actual active batch. The model runner now skips draft proposal only when its request/token threshold state says disabled; it no longer treats an empty scheduled_spec_decode_tokens map as a disable signal, because that can deadlock the first EAGLE draft. Adaptive mode fails fast unless at least one positive static or initial request/token threshold is configured, preventing accidental global SpecDec. ReSpec-style dynamic depth now caps both scheduler lookahead and the draft tokens stored back into scheduler request state by active-batch regime, for example K=3 when active requests <=4, K=2 when active requests <=64, and K=1 otherwise. Dynamic-depth environment variables are now explicitly propagated from NeMo-RL VllmGeneration into Ray actor environments, and the 30B eval wrapper preserves SPECDEC_DYNAMIC_DRAFT_* through wrapper submission. The NeMo-RL step controller now uses per-position acceptance floors: weak position 3 lowers only the small-tail K tier from K=3 to K=2, while weak position 2 lowers all tiers that would use a second draft token. Review commit b40917f now marks aggregate acceptance publishable only when all DP workers report and prevents the step controller from changing K on partial DP metrics.
adaptive_gate_implementation.metrics_visibility: NeMo-RL exposes structured spec_decode_gate metrics in addition to vLLM acceptance counters: scheduler/runner checked, enabled, disabled, enabled_ratio, last scheduled request count, last active request count, last token count, thresholds, adaptive threshold state, dynamic draft-depth state including dynamic_last_selected_tokens and dynamic_last_stored_tokens, and per-position acceptance. The async path now logs SpecDec counters before policy get_logprobs, so Step-level acceptance is preserved even if later Megatron logprob/training fails. The early console summary now prints runner and scheduler gate groups separately and skips empty groups, because job 3066594 showed real runner-side long-tail activation while the previous scheduler-only summary misleadingly printed enabled_ratio=0.
adaptive_gate_implementation.default_fast_eval_plan: Qwen3-30B-A3B K=1, MAX_STEPS=8. Primary token-pressure active-batch run uses request threshold 0, token threshold 2048, adaptive target 0.75. Follow-up long-tail request-gate runs use req32+tok2048 and req64+tok2048 with adaptive target 0.50. ReSpec-style dynamic-depth run uses max K=3, req64+tok2048, active-request caps <=4 -> K3, <=64 -> K2, and larger active batches -> K1. Step-controller follow-up uses the same dynamic-depth profile with NRL_SPECDEC_STEP_ADAPTIVE_CONTROLLER=true.
